LiveCallsProvider: Renders no surface of its own: it is `<CallsProvider>` with the realtime subscription attached, and its whole body is `children` plus a `client.subscribe` in an effect. There is nothing to photograph — what it feeds IS photographed: the ring it delivers, over a page, in video.ring (variants incoming / incoming-desktop / audio-only / outgoing). The headless half is demoed there as `CallsProvider`; this one differs only in where the frames come from, which is not a visual difference.
CallRoute: Composition-only, and unphotographable by construction: it wires `<CallStage>` (which loads an optional WebRTC peer and opens a media session) to `<CallPanel>`, and it renders NOTHING until the provider holds an accepted call AND this browser holds a media grant. A demo could only reach it by standing up a fake SFU, which would photograph the fake. Both halves are photographed on their own: the session's states in video.call-stage (no-peer / no-token) and the call itself in video.call-panel (connected / audio-only / reconnecting).
